links.title: Jaeger File Worker
links.tooltip: Open Jaeger UI for file worker traces

options.content: This dashboard is the x-ray for Telegram file handling. Read it top to bottom: first check the red-flag indicators, then inspect backlog and bytes, then worker flow, latency, discovery, dependencies, and traces. Empty latency graphs mean no matching file activity in the selected window; top stat panels keep missing file telemetry visible as No telemetry. Each file-related metric family has exactly one owner section here and a plain-language entry in Metric Meanings.

panels.description: Current number of file download jobs waiting in Postgres. Short spikes are normal after new file discovery; sustained growth means the worker or TDLib cannot keep up.
panels.title: Queued Jobs

panels.description: Current number of durable file assets in failed state. This should stay at zero in a healthy run; non-zero means files need retry or root-cause inspection.
panels.title: Failed Assets

panels.description: Queued jobs multiplied by a no-worker-tick condition for the selected rate window. Any non-zero value means work exists but the worker did not run.
panels.title: Backlog Without Ticks

panels.description: Rate of worker job outcomes marked failed. This is a direct signal that downloads or canonicalization are failing.
panels.title: Failure Rate

panels.description: Rate of worker retries scheduled because file downloads were deferred while the shared TDLib scheduler was busy. Non-zero explains why queued downloads are waiting without counting deferred jobs as processed jobs.
panels.title: Download Defer Rate

panels.description: Rate of stale downloading jobs reconciled by the watchdog. Non-zero means TDLib completion/update events did not finish the job on the first path.
panels.title: Stale Recovery Rate

panels.description: Current number of downloading jobs older than the worker claim timeout. Any non-zero value means TDLib handoff or completion events are not closing jobs on time.
panels.title: Stale Downloading

panels.description: Age in seconds of the oldest downloading job. This shows how long the queue has been waiting for TDLib progress or worker reconciliation.
panels.title: Oldest Downloading

panels.description: Current failed durable assets grouped by bounded failure reason. This is the first stop after the red Failed Assets tile: not_found points to unavailable Telegram media, stale_retry_limit points to worker/TDLib completion trouble, storage_io points to local canonicalization/storage, and unknown needs log or trace inspection.
panels.title: Failed Assets By Reason

links.title: Open file worker traces in Jaeger

panels.description: Worker failures produced inside the selected dashboard range, grouped by worker source. Use this to separate old durable failed assets from failures still happening now.
panels.title: New Failed Worker Jobs

options.content:
Use `Failure Logs` for assetKey, raw error message, and trace_id. Use `Recent File Worker Traces` for the worker path around reconcile, claim, dispatch, and publish stages.

| Reason | Operator decision |
|---|---|
| `not_found` | Telegram or TDLib says the media is unavailable. Treat as remote-data loss unless the same source later emits a new file id. |
| `stale_retry_limit` | The worker handed work to TDLib and did not observe completion after retry recovery. Inspect worker traces, TDLib queue pressure, and updateFile flow. |
| `missing_tdlib_file_id` | Stored asset cannot be downloaded because the TDLib file id is absent. Treat as a persistence or extraction bug. |
| `storage_io` | Download reached local canonicalization/storage and failed on filesystem I/O. Inspect file server volume and permissions. |
| `unknown` | The raw error did not match a known operational class. Inspect Loki logs and recent file worker traces. |

panels.description: File download failure logs for the selected dashboard range. Open log details to read assetKey, source, transport, error.message, trace_id, and span_id. Empty results mean Loki did not ingest matching failure logs for this range.
panels.title: Failure Logs

panels.description: Recent Jaeger traces for telegram.file.worker.tick in the selected dashboard range. Use trace_id from Failure Logs when investigating one failed asset; use this table when failures are current but the exact trace id is not known.
panels.title: Recent File Worker Traces

links.title: Open file worker traces in Jaeger

panels.description: telegram.file.queue.assets. Durable asset counts by state: known waits for work, ready is canonicalized and usable, failed needs attention.
panels.title: Asset State

panels.description: telegram.file.queue.jobs. Active queue table rows by state: queued waits to be claimed, downloading has been handed to TDLib and waits for completion.
panels.title: Download Jobs

panels.description: telegram.file.queue.bytes. Byte backlog for active queued/downloading jobs where total size is known: downloaded, remaining, and total.
panels.title: Known Bytes

panels.description: telegram.file.queue.unknown_remaining. Active queued/downloading jobs where Telegram has not provided a byte size; bytes panels cannot account for these.
panels.title: Unknown-Size Remaining Files

panels.description: telegram.file.worker.wake. Why the worker was scheduled: startup, enqueue events, updateFile completion, immediate continuation, file-download defer retry, stale watchdog, or error backoff.
panels.title: Wake Reasons

panels.description: telegram.file.worker.jobs. Worker throughput by source and outcome after the worker touched real jobs. File-download defers are wake reasons, not job outcomes.
panels.title: Job Outcomes By Source

panels.description: telegram.file.worker.stage.duration count. How often each worker stage runs: tick, stale reconcile, claim, TDLib dispatch/inspect, canonicalization, and publish changes.
panels.title: Worker Stage Rate

panels.description: telegram.file.worker.stage.duration p95. Where time is spent inside the worker. High dispatch/inspect points to TDLib; high canonicalize points to filesystem/hash/storage; high publish points to state event fanout.
panels.title: Worker Stage P95

panels.description: telegram.file.record.stage.duration count. How often file references are discovered, slots are replaced, stale slots are pruned, and owner/queue changes are published.
panels.title: File Record Stage Rate

panels.description: telegram.file.record.stage.duration p95. Latency of file discovery/materialization before download work exists. High replace_slots means DB/write pressure in file slot persistence.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (telegram_file_record_stage, telegram_file_record_cause, telegram_file_owner_model, le) (rate(telegram_file_record_stage_duration_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: File Record Stage P95

panels.description: telegram.file.generation.outcomes. Outcome rate for TDLib file generation URL fetches. Failed blocked_url means SSRF protection rejected a target before download.
panels.title: Generation Outcomes

panels.description: telegram.file.generation.duration p95. Time spent fetching a generated file URL and writing it to the TDLib destination path.
panels.title: Generation Duration P95

panels.description: RPC server count for the file-facing Dashboard request procedure. Ready file bytes are served by the dedicated file server, not Dashboard RPC.
panels.title: Dashboard File Request RPC Rate

panels.description: RPC server p95 for the file-facing request procedure. High requestFile latency points to policy or DB enqueue pressure.
panels.title: Dashboard File Request RPC P95

panels.description: App DB operation rate for queries touching file subsystem tables. This is the DB x-ray for file queue and asset/slot storage load.
panels.title: File DB Query Rate

panels.description: App DB p95 for file subsystem tables. Use this with File DB Query Rate to confirm whether file queue changes are causing DB pressure.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (service_name, db_query_summary, le) (rate(db_client_operation_duration_seconds_bucket{service_name=~"telegram|dashboard-server", db_system_name="postgresql", db_query_summary=~".*telegram_file_.*|.*telegram_tdlib_files.*"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: File DB Query P95

panels.description: Rate of telegram.files.* NATS publishes. queueChanged wakes the file worker and mounted UI state; ownerChanged tells views that file references changed.
panels.title: File Events Send Rate

panels.description: P95 latency for publishing telegram.files.* events. High values mean file state publication itself is slow before subscribers can react.
panels.title: File Events Send P95

panels.description: Rate of telegram.files.* event handling by subscribers. Use it with send rate to see whether subscribers are actually consuming file state changes.
panels.title: File Events Process Rate

panels.description: P95 latency for processing telegram.files.* events. High values mean file queue/owner changes are published but subscribers are slow to apply them.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (service_name, messaging_destination_name, messaging_destination_subscription_name, le) (rate(messaging_process_duration_seconds_bucket{messaging_system="nats", messaging_destination_name=~"telegram[.]files[.].*"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: File Events Process P95

options.content:
| Metric family | Where it lives | What it answers | Bad sign |
|---|---|---|---|
| `telegram.file.queue.assets` | Current State, Backlog And Bytes | How many durable file assets are known, ready, or failed. | `failed > 0` or `known` grows while jobs do not move. |
| `telegram.file.queue.failures` | Failed Assets Triage | How many failed durable assets exist by bounded failure reason. | Any non-zero reason count needs retry or root-cause inspection. |
| `telegram.file.queue.jobs` | Current State, Backlog And Bytes | How many download jobs are queued or already handed to TDLib. | `queued` grows or `downloading` stays high without ready/failed outcomes. |
| `telegram.file.queue.stale_downloading` | Current State | How many downloading jobs are older than the worker claim timeout. | Any non-zero value means the stale watchdog is needed to recover active work. |
| `telegram.file.queue.oldest_downloading_age` | Current State | Age in seconds of the oldest downloading job. | Values above the claim timeout mean TDLib progress or worker reconciliation is late. |
| `telegram.file.queue.bytes` | Backlog And Bytes | Known downloaded, remaining, and total bytes for active jobs. | Remaining bytes grows while worker job rate is flat. |
| `telegram.file.queue.unknown_remaining` | Backlog And Bytes | Active jobs whose size is unknown, so byte panels undercount backlog. | High value means the byte x-ray is incomplete. |
| `telegram.file.generation.outcomes` | File Generation | Whether TDLib URL generation completed, failed, or was aborted. | `failed blocked_url` means SSRF protection rejected a target; other failures mean fetch/write trouble. |
| `telegram.file.generation.duration` | File Generation | Time spent fetching a generated file URL and writing it to TDLib destination storage. | High p95 means generation fetch or filesystem writes are slow. |
| `telegram.file.worker.wake` | Worker Flow | Why the worker was scheduled. | `file_download_defer` or `failure_backoff` dominates. |
| `telegram.file.worker.jobs` | Current State, Worker Flow | What happened to jobs after the worker touched them. | `failed` or `stale` dominates `ready`. |
| `telegram.file.worker.stage.duration` | Current State, Worker Flow | How often each worker stage runs and where worker time is spent. | High `dispatch_tdlib`, `canonicalize_completed`, or `publish_changes`. |
| `telegram.file.record.stage.duration` | File Discovery And Record Path | Time spent discovering, materializing, pruning, and publishing file slots before downloads exist. | High `replace_slots` or `publish_changes`. |
| `rpc.server.call.duration` filtered to `telegram.dashboard.requestFile` | Boundaries And Storage | Manual file request rate and latency. | High `requestFile` points to enqueue, policy, or DB pressure. |
| `db.client.operation.duration` filtered to file tables | Boundaries And Storage | DB load and latency from file queue, asset, slot, and TDLib file tables. | High rate with high p95 means file storage is the DB pressure source. |
| `messaging.client.operation.duration` filtered to `telegram.files.*` | Boundaries And Storage | Rate and latency of publishing file queue/owner state changes. | High p95 means state changes are slow before subscribers see them. |
| `messaging.process.duration` filtered to `telegram.files.*` | Boundaries And Storage | Rate and latency of subscribers applying file queue/owner events. | Send rate without process rate, or high process p95. |
